title: tokens.css missing brand-refresh tokens — --accent / --caro-* never landed
description:
Discovered during caro-5a2 footer fix audit (2026-04-28).

The PR #993 brand-refresh narrative claims that website/src/ui/tokens.css became the single source of truth with new Caro brand primitives (`--caro-grey-*`, `--caro-beige-*`, `--caro-red-*`, `--caro-yellow-*`), semantic tokens (`--bg`, `--accent`, `--font-display`, `--track-widest`, etc.), Figtree @font-face block, and Azeret Mono @import.

**Reality check (verified via grep):**
- `grep -- '--accent:' website/src/ui/tokens.css` → 0 hits
- `grep -- '--caro-grey-900' website/src/ui/tokens.css` → 0 hits
- `grep -- '--caro-beige-100' website/src/ui/tokens.css` → 0 hits
- File still has `--color-primary: #ff8c42` (deprecated orange) at line 12
- File still has `--color-error: #ef4444` (Tailwind red collision) at line 22
- File still has `--color-bg-tertiary: #fff8f0` (warm-amber, was supposed to be #faf8ec)
- 228 lines total, no Caro brand primitives, no @font-face for Figtree

**Why this matters:**
- PR #993 review burden: the 'foundational' rebrand foundation isn't actually in the canonical token file. Components reference `var(--accent, #ef3333)` with fallback — the fallback works defensively, but the design-system contract is broken.
- Future drift: any developer reading `tokens.css` to learn the brand sees the OLD brand. New components will use the wrong tokens.
- Single source of truth violated: brand colors are scattered across LP*.astro components instead of centralized.

**Investigation needed:**
1. Check git log for tokens.css on the great-davinci-b17c9b branch (PR #993). Did the brand tokens land in commits and then get reverted? Or did they never land?
2. Compare the current tokens.css against what was specified in the original brand-refresh plan.

**Fix scope:**
- Restore the missing brand primitives + semantic tokens to tokens.css per the original plan
- Sweep `--color-primary: #ff8c42` → `var(--accent)` site-wide, OR redefine `--color-primary` to alias `var(--accent)` for backward compat
- Add the Figtree @font-face block (fonts already in website/public/fonts/)
- Add Azeret Mono @import

**Blocks:** PR #993 review/merge if the rebrand is meant to ship as a 'foundation'. Could ship as-is and follow up, but that creates an awkward 'foundation that doesn't exist in the token file' state.

Discovered by: claude-design-frontend-engineer audit (gap #5 in caro-5a2 report).

title: Emoji-to-pixel-icon migration — request deferred v3 icons from Claude Design
description:

- Pixel grid trades realism for character — brain at 16x16 is hard

Broader glyph family: she'll do a considered pass for the named surfaces (rocket/shield/lightning/brain/dog-mark) but stop short of a full Lucide replacement. Scope stays honest.

Inventory of emoji-as-feature-glyph usages (high-priority surfaces):

Now unblocked: see follow-up issue for ingest + emoji-replacement migration.

title: Migrate reqwest 0.11 → 0.12 (unblocks RUSTSEC-2026-{0098,0099,0104} legacy path)
description:
**Discovered:** 2026-04-29 during caro-871 cargo-update triage by background agent.

The 3 RUSTSEC advisories blocking Security Audit on every PR cannot be fully resolved via lockfile updates because reqwest 0.11.x → rustls 0.21.x → rustls-webpki 0.101.7 has no upstream patch path. The fix versions (>=0.103.12) are SemVer-incompatible with the 0.101 line; rustls 0.21.12 is terminal (last release).

**The migration:**
- Bump Cargo.toml:49: `reqwest = "0.11"` → `"0.12"`
- Touch 8+ files in src/:
  - backends/remote/* (HTTP client construction)
  - cache/* (download/upload)
  - knowledge/indexers/github.rs
  - cli/mod.rs
  - doctor.rs
- chromadb 2.3.0 also pins reqwest 0.11 transitively — may need to vendor or wait for chromadb 3.x

**API breaks 0.11 → 0.12:**
- Body type changes (Body::wrap_stream signature)
- Some builder methods are async vs sync
- TLS provider selection changes (rustls vs native-tls feature flag mapping)
- Reference: https://github.com/seanmonstar/reqwest/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#v0120

**Why this matters:**
- Long-term: vulnerability surface stays smaller after migration
- Short-term: not blocking — partial fix + audit.toml ignore matches existing project precedent (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, RUSTSEC-2026-0009 both ignored for the same reason)

**Sequencing:**
1. caro-871 ships short-term unblock (audit.toml ignore + partial cargo update for modern path)
2. This issue is the long-term fix; no rush
3. When chromadb upstream releases a reqwest-0.12-compatible version, revisit transitive coverage

**Estimate:** 1-2 days incl. testing.

**Branch ready to resume:** `chore/cargo-update-rustsec` exists locally in worktree at .claude/worktrees/cargo-update-rustsec with the partial-fix change reverted. Re-apply the cargo update -p rustls-webpki@0.103.10 to start.

title: Main CI broken: ChromaDB Integration Tests + Security Audit failing on every PR
description:
Discovered while triaging PR #1006 / PR #1007 CI on 2026-04-29. Both PRs (entirely unrelated code: footer color tokens vs Astro icon SVGs) fail the same 2 of 50 checks at identical labels. Confirmed via gh run view --log-failed.

**Failure 1 — ChromaDB Integration Tests** (job 73510317519 / 73514317080):
- 'ChromaDB failed to become healthy' — service startup flake in the GH Actions runner
- Cascading: 'assertion left == right failed: Should have 10 entries after recording 10 commands'
- Infrastructure: ChromaDB container doesn't reach ready state in CI's available time window
- Affected tests: chromadb_tests::test_chromadb_multiple_operations + others

**Failure 2 — Security Audit** (job 73510317540 / 73514317057):
- cargo-audit flags 3 RUSTSEC advisories in Cargo.lock:
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0098
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0099
  - RUSTSEC-2026-0104
- Each appears multiple times (transitive deps via gix or similar)

**Impact:**
- All PRs fail required-check gates
- 200 dependabot vulnerabilities mentioned in remote push output (separate issue but related lift)
- Slows merge cadence

**Fix paths:**
1. Security Audit: open a chore(deps) PR running 'cargo update' against the 3 RUSTSECs. Verify with cargo-audit --deny=warnings locally first.
2. ChromaDB Integration: make the service-startup wait more generous, OR convert to continue-on-error if the test isn't in the merge gate, OR move to a nightly run.
3. After both green on main, PRs #1006 and #1007 can merge cleanly.

**Discovered by:** PR triage during caro-y5i visual audit cycle.

The v2.1 kyaro-mark glyph from Claude Design's icon pack does not read as the intended kawaii Shiba — at every render size (16/20/32 px) the silhouette shows two sharp upward triangles parsing as horns or upright cat-ears, a centered face bracket, and no visible muzzle/tongue.

PR #1007 wires this glyph into Footer.astro replacing the 🐕 emoji at the brand-link header AND in the kyaro-banner mascot section. The Footer renders on EVERY subpage of caro.sh. If merged unchanged, every page on caro.sh shows what reads as a horned-demon Caro icon — an immediate brand-fidelity regression that contradicts the brand-book's stated 'goodest office dog' tribute.

**Evidence (saved screenshots in this worktree):**
- audit-desktop-1440.png (footer 20 px and 32 px sections)
- audit-mobile-390.png

**Mitigation paths for THIS PR (any one suffices):**
1. Revert Footer.astro to 🐕 emoji; keep kyaro-mark in manifest for v2.1.1 use only.
2. Replace kyaro-mark in Footer.astro with the existing mark-caro-pixel.png (which IS a recognizable Shiba face).
3. Hold #1007 entirely until Claude Design ships v2.1.1 kyaro-mark.

**Forward path:**
- Dispatch claude-design-frontend-engineer to draft a deferential message to Claude Design at https://claude.ai/design/p/332f73e9-… surfacing the kyaro-mark readability finding with the audit screenshots attached (her workspace supports image upload). Treat as design feedback for a v2.1.1, not a defect blame.
- Cite Claude Design's own concession in v2.1: she flagged that the brain glyph 'reads slightly helmet-y at 32 px'. Brain is a known-soft area; kyaro-mark wasn't flagged but should have been. Use her own framing as scaffolding for the kyaro-mark feedback.

**Closure criterion:**
- Either kyaro-mark redrawn by Claude Design, OR Footer.astro reverted in PR #1007 (with manifest entry retained for future v2.1.1 swap).

Blocks: PR #1007 merge.

title: [brand][design-feedback] Gaps in caro-design-system to surface to claude.ai/design
description:
Track design-system gaps encountered during the long-tail migration to send back to claude.ai/design as feedback. Initial gaps:

1. **No dark-mode tokens**: brand guideline only specifies light (paper-and-ink). Site has a .dark theme with overrides; the design system doesn't tell us what dark-mode brand looks like. Currently improvising.

2. **Status colors**: design-system defines status-safe / status-warn / status-danger / status-critical, but the website code uses --color-info / --color-warning / --color-success and --color-error too. Recommend: expand status palette to cover info (blue) and success (green) explicitly, OR remove those from semantic tokens.

3. **Support-pink (#ea4aaa)**: heart Support links use a magenta the brand book doesn't mention. Either (a) add a 'support-pink' brand token, or (b) replace with brand red.

4. **Holiday themes (Christmas, Hanukkah, Diwali, NewYear, etc.)**: existing seasonal overlays not addressed by brand book. Out of scope for foundational rebrand but flag for the brand team.

5. **No pixel-icon system**: brand book names 4 icons (Home, Location, Teams, Tools) but artwork wasn't shipped. Site uses emoji feature glyphs as fallback.

6. **No SVG logo source files**: only PNGs available. Recommend shipping .svg or .ai for crisp scaling.

7. **Azeret Mono not bundled**: loaded from Google Fonts. Recommend shipping TTFs locally for offline / privacy.

When this list grows, post a single comment on the design conversation referencing it.
notes:
Additional gaps surfaced during the long-tail migration (PR #993 expansion, 96 files):

8. **Non-status semantic colors not defined**: Brand book covers status (safe/warn/danger/critical) but the codebase uses --color-info (#3b82f6), --color-success (#22c55e), --color-warning (#f59e0b), --color-error (#ef4444) too. These are NOT in the design system. Recommend: extend palette OR explicitly tell consumers to alias status-* to those.

9. **--color-bg-tertiary peach (#fff8f0)**: Used in code blocks and accent panels across the site. Not in the brand book. Should it be replaced by --bg-subtle (caro-beige-50)?

10. **--color-primary-light (#ffa76c → #f56565)**: Brand book defines primary-only red. The codebase needed a 'lighter primary' for hover surface tints (e.g. card hover backgrounds). We chose #f56565; brand should bless or replace.

11. **Per-distro accent theming**: Site has --distro-accent: #ef3333 (default) overridden per OS/distro (Ubuntu purple, macOS gradient, etc.). Not addressed by brand book — should distros override the brand red, or stay neutral?

12. **Card hover-tint shadow recipe**: ~30 components use rgba(255,140,66,0.15-0.3) for hover lift shadows. We mechanically converted to rgba(239,51,51,X). Brand should specify a canonical shadow recipe (paper-and-ink should arguably stay solid, no shadows).

13. **Comparison-page outline buttons**: Page templates use border + color of brand red, often combined with peach background. Looks too 'warning' for a happy-path CTA. Brand should define a non-CTA outline button style.

14. **Charts/visualizations**: Some pages have inline SVG fills referencing --color-primary or hard-coded oranges. The brand book doesn't address chart palettes. Recommend: define a chart-safe sequential palette (OK to layer on top of the 4 brand colors but needs to be specified).

15. **Storybook theme**: .storybook/theme.ts referenced colorPrimary/colorSecondary directly. Is there a brand way to theme Storybook chrome that the design system should ship?

When this list reaches ~20 items, post a single comment on the original design conversation referencing it as v2 feedback.
close_reason: Posted as a structured 12-finding feedback message to claude.ai/design Caro Design System conversation. Claude Design responded with a full v2 update covering: dark-mode token layer, semantic feedback colors (info/success/warning/error distinct from status-*), --bg-tertiary canonized to #faf8ec, --accent-tint + --accent-light, --shadow-card-hover, --focus-ring, chart palette (--chart-1..8 categorical + --chart-seq-0..5 sequential), --distro-accent with explicit contract, --link-visited (desaturated plum, WCAG 1.4.1). Plus README additions: section-color ratio rule, holiday overlays recipe, Storybook theme spec, indicatif #RRGGBB note, voice update banning blazing-fast, v2 changelog. New preview cards: Colors · Dark mode, Colors · Semantic feedback, Colors · Chart palette. Deferred to v3: diverging chart palette, pixel iconography, bundled Azeret Mono, Newsletter/Logo Pack figmas.

title: Vercel SSO blocks design-auditor agents from preview deploys
description:
PR #1007 visual audit on 2026-04-29 was blocked at https://caro-foss-website-git-feat-icon-pack-v21-ingest-kadosh-dev.vercel.app/ — Vercel returned HTTP 401 because the kadosh-dev Vercel project enables SSO Protection. Audit fell back to a static render of PR-branch SVGs which lacks real Footer/Hero chrome.

**Impact:** every PR's design-auditor agent loses the ability to verify glyphs/colors/spacing in real production-equivalent context. Audit fidelity drops from 95% to ~70% (icons render, but parent component context — gradients, dark-mode swaps, hover states, z-index layering — all unchecked).

**Fix paths:**
1. Vercel project settings → Disable SSO Protection on PR previews (production deploy stays gated).
2. OR generate per-PR _vercel_share= bypass tokens via Vercel CLI and post in PR description so unauthenticated agents/reviewers can view.
3. OR add the agent's Vercel team email to the SSO allowlist (org-dependent).

Path 1 is preferred for OSS workflows: PR previews on a public repo should be public.

**Discovered by:** claude-design-frontend-engineer audit cycle on PR #1007.

title: Cards & boxes — align all surfaces to brand-book card spec
description:
User reports cards/boxes do not match brand-book styling rules. The brand-book card spec (per the implementation we did in LPHero install panel and LPDownload):

**Default:**
- background: `var(--bg-raised)` (paper-tinted lift)
- border: 1 px solid `var(--border)`
- radius: `var(--radius-lg)` (8 px)
- shadow: `var(--shadow-1)` at rest

**Hover:**
- transform: translateY(-4px)
- box-shadow: `var(--shadow-3)`
- border-color: `var(--accent)`
- **Never** scale (transform: scale(...)) — flagged as anti-pattern in brand book

**Forbidden:**
- Left-accent stripe borders (`border-left: 4px solid var(--accent)`)
- Gradient backgrounds on default cards (gradients reserved for hero CTA only)
- Shadow-on-rest values darker than `var(--shadow-1)`

**Audit targets:**
- LPMoments.astro — card grid
- LPTestimonials.astro — testimonial cards (already has hover lift, verify)
- LPPersonas.astro — persona cards
- LPDifferentiators.astro — comparison cards
- LPScenarios.astro — scenario cards
- LPBestPractices.astro — practice cards
- LPWaitlist.astro — waitlist card
- Any component using `border-left:` for accent

**Workflow:**
1. claude-design-frontend-engineer audits each component against the spec
2. Reports gaps as a single combined punchlist
3. Implementation follows in a single migration commit per component family
4. tokens.css may need new tokens (e.g. `--bg-raised-hover`) — verify with Claude Design before adding

title: Ingest v2.1 pixel icons from Claude Design + replace emoji on flagged surfaces
description:
Claude Design shipped v2.1 of the Caro design system on 2026-04-28 with nine pixel icons that close caro-0qp. Files live in her design-system workspace at assets/icons/ — they need to be pulled into the caro repo and wired into the website + (optionally) CLI surfaces.

Deliverables in her workspace:
- assets/icons/home.svg
- assets/icons/location.svg
- assets/icons/teams.svg
- assets/icons/tools.svg
- assets/icons/rocket.svg
- assets/icons/shield.svg
- assets/icons/lightning.svg
- assets/icons/brain.svg
- assets/icons/kyaro-mark.svg
- assets/icons/manifest.json (category, replaced-emoji, tier)
- Preview card "Brand · Pixel icons" registered in the Design System tab

Specs (must preserve in repo):
- 16x16 logical grid, integer pixels, shape-rendering: crispEdges, monochrome via currentColor
- Render at 16/24/32/48px (default 2x for crispness)
- Recolor through token: color: var(--fg-strong) — survives dark mode automatically
- No hardcoded fills (inherit from parent only)

Tasks:
1. Pull the 9 SVGs + manifest.json from Claude Design's workspace into website/public/icons/ (or website/src/assets/icons/, per existing convention).
2. Add a small <Glyph name="..." size={24} /> Astro component that wraps inline SVG via <use href> + sets color: var(--fg-strong).
3. Replace emoji on flagged surfaces:
   - LPHero.astro trust badges: 🚀 → rocket, 🛡️ → shield, ⚡ → lightning
   - LPPersonas.astro: persona icons → home/location/teams/tools (verify mapping with author)
   - LPMoments.astro: feature glyphs → rocket/shield/lightning/brain (per manifest)
   - LPBestPractices.astro: bullet markers → tools/lightning/etc.
   - LPDifferentiators.astro: comparison icons
   - Footer.astro 🐕: → kyaro-mark glyph (NOT the full Kyaro sprite — this is for inline runs)
4. Do NOT remove emoji until the swap is wired and verified visually — Glyph component should fall back gracefully.
5. Verify caro.sh dark-mode renders correctly (icons should pick up --fg-strong on .dark via currentColor).

Out of scope (her v3 backlog, deferred):
- git, terminal, package, model, gear, doc, search, spinner, check, cross icons
- PNG raster sprites @1x/2x/3x (request from her if indicatif or any non-SVG surface needs them)

Caveats noted by her:
- Brain reads slightly helmet-y at 32px — acceptable; worth a designer's-eye revisit if it lands awkwardly in production.
- Kyaro-mark is a glyph, not a portrait. Use full Kyaro GIFs for hero/decision moments only.

Closes caro-0qp on completion.

Gaps (kept as emoji — no v2.1 counterpart):

Verification:
- npm run build → passes (58 pages)

Will mark closed once PR merges.
